predecessors.name: Byzantine Empire
predecessors.text: the island of Euboea, established 'after the partition of the Byzantine Empire following the Fourth Crusade' (Triarchy page)

successors.name: Ottoman Empire
successors.text: the whole island, after Mehmed II took Chalkis on 12 July 1470

ledger.x: 1204: Euboea becomes a crusader fief after the partition of the Byzantine Empire.

Mid-1205: Jacques of Avesnes dies and Euboea passes to three Veronese barons: Ravano dalle Carceri, Giberto dalle Carceri and Pecoraro da Mercanuovo, who split it into Oreos (north), Karystos (south) and Chalkis (central); Chalkis was the shared capital.
June 1256: two triarchs break with Achaea.

Early 1258: Venice retakes Chalkis, which William had captured; the Achaean victory at Karydi (May/June 1258) ends the war on the mainland, Doge Reniero Zeno negotiates peace in 1259 and a 1262 treaty recognises William's suzerainty.
1278: Licario's Byzantine occupation of most of Euboea.
By 1296: Boniface of Verona has expelled the Byzantines from Euboea.
1317: Karystos falls to the Catalan Company.
1365: Venice acquires Karystos, reuniting the island.

1390: the last triarch's lands pass to Venice and Negroponte becomes a Venetian colony. the last triarchs died in 1383 and 1390 and left their lands to Venice; infobox 'protectorate of Venice, 1209-1390; then a Venetian colony, 1390-1470'.
12 July 1470: Negroponte ends with the Ottoman conquest of Chalkis.

wars.name: Lombard rebellion against Henry of Flanders
wars.outcome: Ravano dalle Carceri allied with the failed Lombard revolt, then in March 1209 recognised Venetian overlordship and in May 1209 acknowledged vassalage to the Latin Empire; Henry ended the feudal dependency of Negroponte on Thessalonica in 1208-09.

wars.name: War of the Euboeote Succession
wars.outcome: William II of Villehardouin captured Chalkis, Venice retook it in early 1258, William won at Karydi in May/June 1258, Doge Reniero Zeno negotiated peace in 1259 and a 1262 treaty recognised William's suzerainty over the triarchs.

wars.name: Byzantine campaigns on Euboea under Licario
wars.outcome: Licario left after 1280 and by 1296 Boniface of Verona had expelled the Byzantines from Euboea.

wars.name: Catalan Company's conquest of Karystos
wars.outcome: Karystos fell to the Catalan Company in 1317 and a 1319 treaty let Don Alfonso keep it; Venice bought it in 1365.

wars.name: Ottoman conquest of Negroponte
wars.outcome: On 12 July 1470 Mehmed II took Chalkis and the whole island came under Ottoman control.

certainty.note: An island: its coast is its border.
